library/seo-slug-generator.yml.when_to_use: When the user needs to turn a page title or article text into a clean lowercase hyphenated URL slug.

patterns/agent-with-tools.yml.summary_en: A ReAct-style Agent node takes a user query, calls registered plugin tools to gather what it needs, and returns a synthesized answer.
patterns/agent-with-tools.yml.when_to_use: When the user wants an autonomous agent that decides which tools to call to answer an open-ended query.
patterns/agent-with-tools.yml.gotchas: Skeleton ships with empty model and empty tools list plus empty dependencies[]; register plugin tools and pick a strong tool-use model before it runs. Curated pattern — copy-paste-ready seed for this shape.

patterns/chatwork-1-10-20.yml.summary_en: A scheduled, unattended job that ingests items from MULTIPLE sources (custom-auth HTTP attachments read by a Vision LLM, plus a web-search tool), merges them by a priority rule, ranks a top-N shortlist with an LLM, writes each item up with an LLM, dedupes against an existing spreadsheet, appends only new rows, and notifies just when there is something new.
patterns/chatwork-1-10-20.yml.when_to_use: When a recurring job with no operator present must gather from more than one source, rank to a shortlist, have an LLM write each item up, and append to a running log (Google Sheet) without duplicating past entries — notifying only on non-empty results.
patterns/chatwork-1-10-20.yml.gotchas: Empty LLM models ship by design (wire a model per node; the image node MUST be Vision-capable). Schedule trigger timezone defaults to UTC — set Asia/Tokyo explicitly. Custom auth header uses authorization:{type:no-auth} + the token in headers via a secret env var (api-key auth types rewrite headers). Both iterations use continue-on-error so one bad item never stalls the run. Idempotency comes from reading existing sheet rows and deduping before append. 17 # TODO customization points (source API, room/keywords, sheet range, extraction prompt, fire time). Curated pattern distilled from a proven build (spec 052).

patterns/file-iteration.yml.summary_en: Upload a structured file, extract its text, split it into items, process each item in a parallel iteration, then aggregate the per-item results into one output.
patterns/file-iteration.yml.when_to_use: When the user wants to upload a CSV/JSON/text file and run the same per-row processing over every item, then collect the results.
patterns/file-iteration.yml.gotchas: The per-item processor is a passthrough Code node — swap it for LLM/HTTP/Tool. Iteration is capped at 30 items; tune parallel_nums to your API limits. Curated pattern — copy-paste-ready seed for this shape.

patterns/file-to-llm.yml.summary_en: Upload one file, extract its text with a document extractor, run a single LLM call over it, and return the result.
patterns/file-to-llm.yml.when_to_use: When the user wants to do one LLM task (summarize, translate, classify, extract) over the text of a single uploaded file.
patterns/file-to-llm.yml.gotchas: Model provider/name and the LLM dependency hash are blank — fill them from templates/tool-catalog.json before running. The system prompt is a placeholder that must be replaced with the real instruction. Curated pattern — copy-paste-ready seed for this shape.

patterns/meta-workflow-builder.yml.summary_en: From a natural-language requirement, an LLM planner emits a JSON plan, a Code node renders it into a new Dify workflow YAML, and an HTTP request auto-imports the generated app into the local workspace.
patterns/meta-workflow-builder.yml.when_to_use: When the user wants Dify to generate and auto-import a new workflow from a plain-language description of what it should do.
patterns/meta-workflow-builder.yml.gotchas: V1 only generates the file-to-llm shape; the Code node uses stdlib only (no yaml lib). Requires DIFY_CONSOLE_URL and a valid DIFY_CONSOLE_TOKEN bearer token in environment_variables. Curated pattern — copy-paste-ready seed for this shape.

patterns/multi-step-llm.yml.summary_en: Chains three LLM calls where each output feeds the next — an initial generation, a critique, then a refinement — to produce a polished final result.
patterns/multi-step-llm.yml.when_to_use: When the user wants an iterative generate-critique-refine LLM chain, such as translate-then-improve or outline-draft-polish.
patterns/multi-step-llm.yml.gotchas: All three model slots are blank placeholders — configure provider/name (a cheaper model for critique, a stronger one for the final step). Curated pattern — copy-paste-ready seed for this shape.

patterns/per-row-notify-excel.yml.summary_en: Operator uploads a rows Excel and a key-to-destination mapping Excel; the flow extracts and parses both in-flow, then for each row judges whether to act and POSTs an LLM-composed message to the mapped destination.
patterns/per-row-notify-excel.yml.when_to_use: When the user has Excel files of rows and destinations and wants a per-row conditional notification sent to each matching row's destination.
patterns/per-row-notify-excel.yml.gotchas: Document extractor renders xlsx as a markdown table — cells with literal '|' split wrong; NAME_COL/TARGET_COL and the judge rule must match your sheet. Iteration is capped at 30 items and the flow is NOT idempotent (re-runs re-notify). Curated pattern — copy-paste-ready seed for this shape.

patterns/per-row-notify.yml.summary_en: Takes a JSON rows array, a destination map, and a run date, iterates each row to judge whether to act, and POSTs an LLM-composed message to the per-row destination, aggregating the results.
patterns/per-row-notify.yml.when_to_use: When the user has a list of rows plus a destination map and wants a per-row conditional notification dispatched to each matching row's endpoint.
patterns/per-row-notify.yml.gotchas: Pass `today` in from the caller — in-sandbox dates drift with timezone. Custom-header services need authorization no-auth with the token in headers via an env secret. Not idempotent — re-runs re-notify. Curated pattern — copy-paste-ready seed for this shape.

patterns/rag-qa.yml.summary_en: Answers a user question grounded in a knowledge base: a knowledge-retrieval node fetches relevant chunks and an LLM composes a cited answer from that context.
patterns/rag-qa.yml.when_to_use: When the user wants questions answered strictly from an uploaded knowledge base with citations and a no-answer fallback.
patterns/rag-qa.yml.gotchas: dataset_ids is empty — fill it with real dataset UUIDs from your workspace, and the LLM model slot is blank. Retrieval mode/top_k/reranking are defaults to tune. Curated pattern — copy-paste-ready seed for this shape.

patterns/scheduled-fetch-notify.yml.summary_en: A schedule trigger fires on a cadence with no operator, GETs data over HTTP, defensively parses it, has an LLM compose a short notification, and POSTs it to a notify service.
patterns/scheduled-fetch-notify.yml.when_to_use: When the user wants a recurring, unattended report or reminder that fetches data and posts a summary notification by itself.
patterns/scheduled-fetch-notify.yml.gotchas: Schedule triggers default to UTC — set timezone (Asia/Tokyo) explicitly or a 9AM JST job fires at 18:00. Publishing alone won't fire it; enable the trigger in Dify Studio. At most one schedule trigger per workflow; every input must be machine-fetchable. Curated pattern — copy-paste-ready seed for this shape.

patterns/scheduled-tool-append.yml.summary_en: A schedule trigger fires unattended, GETs source data over HTTP, a Code node shapes rows, an LLM composes text, and a Dify marketplace tool (Google Sheets batch_update) writes the result into a real SaaS.
patterns/scheduled-tool-append.yml.when_to_use: When the user wants a recurring unattended job that lands data in a real service (spreadsheet, Slack, Notion) via a catalogued Dify tool.
patterns/scheduled-tool-append.yml.gotchas: dependencies[] is intentionally filled and must stay filled — with an empty array the tool node fails silently at runtime. Tool node uses provider_type builtin with the full 3-segment provider_name doubled from provider_id. Timezone must be explicit; enable the trigger in Studio; tool credentials remain the user's setup. Curated pattern — copy-paste-ready seed for this shape.

patterns/webhook-per-row-notify.yml.summary_en: A webhook trigger receives a pushed batch (rows, id-map, today), a Code node parses and filters target rows resolving a destination each, then an iteration composes an LLM message per row and POSTs it, aggregating send counts.
patterns/webhook-per-row-notify.yml.when_to_use: When an external system pushes a batch of rows to Dify over a webhook and the user wants a per-row message sent to each row's resolved destination.
patterns/webhook-per-row-notify.yml.gotchas: Webhook bodies arrive as strings — parse inside a Code node with try/except, never assume valid JSON. Pass `today` from the caller; custom auth headers need no-auth + env-secret token; iteration uses continue-on-error so failed rows drop from counts. Enable the trigger in Studio after import. Curated pattern — copy-paste-ready seed for this shape.
